name: Delaplex Limited
sector: Software services, cloud and supply-chain implementation
summary: Debt-free software-services group with a cash cushion, but FY2026 is not a clean AI-led growth inflection. Revenue rose only 2%, owner profit 5.2%, and core EBITDA excluding other income declined 3.47%. Related US channels remain 58.2% of group sales. Platform investment and UK acquisitions might broaden demand, but unamortized development costs, FX cash-flow classification and new acquisition economics require valuation caution. Quality watchlist, not a buy recommendation. [S1][S6]
identity_note: NSE SME listing and ISIN verified against annual report, June allotment and official security/market data.
score_note: Medium-confidence BQS/Growth Quality; IAS NS. Full canonical audit supplied. No severe governance or financial-reliability override inferred from immaterial drafting differences.

GOV.reason: Transactions and corrections are disclosed, with no severe abuse established. Related customer dependence, low-price options and internally inconsistent option movement/utilization narrative limit assurance. Approval ceilings are not actual deployment.

MOAT.reason: Enterprise software/domain implementation expertise and sticky related-client channels provide continuity. Very high historical concentration, AI pricing pressure and no demonstrated independent pricing power limit defensibility.

REV.reason: Comparable parent five-year CAGR about 9.4% maps to 4. Acquired UK operations are excluded from the organic proxy. Latest parent growth 1.81% and three years near-flat prevent upward adjustment; no automatic penalty solely from consolidation.

DUR.reason: Supply-chain implementation, domestic diversification and paid BSNL pilots support avenues for growth. New acquisition/customer adoption and unquantified pilot conversion prevent treating the runway as contracted.

CAP.reason: Core EBIT fell while platform WIP and acquisition capital grew. Debt-free funding is a positive, but commercial returns on substantial unamortized WIP and acquired goodwill remain unproven. No persistent <=3 override.

CASH.reason: Two-year group conversion is 0.88 x and FY2026 reported FCF positive, with improved parent collections. Historical parent CFO is uneven and FX/asset classification prevents awarding full cash-conversion credit.

BAL.reason: No reported debt and substantial deposits provide resilience even excluding earmarked funds. New acquisition and development commitments plus uncertain deposit availability prevent maximal score.

EXEC.reason: Domestic sales/pilot/acquisition delivery is real, but export contraction, near-flat organic sales and weaker-than-framed H2 reduce confidence in scalable execution. Marketing opportunities are not counted as delivered orders.

EARN.reason: Owner PAT grows 5.2% while core EBITDA falls 3.47%, deposit interest/FX cushion results and platform capitalization defers expenses. Earnings remain positive, preventing a distress score.

L.reason: Observed-only 59-session official turnover implies roughly 12 days at 5%, starting in the 3–4 band. Use the lower score because ESM Stage I, fewer than 100 PANs, a ₹93,420 lot and unverified depth do not support orderly execution. One missing date is not assumed zero.

R.reason: Sensitivity models are reproducible but current available cash, platform cash classification and new-acquisition normalized earnings lack adequate valuation confidence. Do not convert scenario assumptions into point scores. Reassessed against the corrected opening-claim cash/debt cases dated 20 October 2026; the identified material evidence gaps remain, so this factor is still NS.

Closing cash reconciles and audit unmodified; FX/capitalization classification limits normalized cash valuation, not automatic critical hold.

Debt-free March balances and deposits support resilience, but current usable deposits, acquisition payment/fees and development funding are not verified. Severe scenarios may require new facilities; no default or demonstrated unfinanceable shortfall is established. sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Debt-free software-services group with a cash cushion, but FY2026 is not a clean AI-led growth inflection. Revenue rose only 2%, owner profit 5.2%, and core EBITDA excluding other income declined 3.47%. Related US channels remain 58.2% of group sales. Platform investment and UK acquisitions might broaden demand, but unamortized development costs, FX cash-flow classification and new acquisition economics require valuation caution. Quality watchlist, not a buy recommendation. [S1][S6]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Delaplex Limited, INE0SK801018, DELAPLEX, NSE SME, listed 2 February 2024. Group includes UK/Blueberry and 70%-held CelestiaCrew, so parent history is the cleaner organic revenue proxy. Cutoff 20 October 2026. Official 19 October closeRs 155.70, lot 600. Five-year horizon,15% nominal pre-tax hurdle andRs 5 lakh illustrative position. Latest issued shares 9,158,480 follows June allotment, not March capital. [S1][S7][S9][S10]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical BQS and Growth Quality scores are supported with medium confidence, as detailed in factor audits; IAS remains NS. No integrity-fail or critical-reliability override is imposed merely for drafting errors. Audit is unmodified and cash closing balance reconciles, but operating/investing classifications and dilution inconsistencies warrant caution. ESM is an execution restriction, not proof of misconduct. [S1][S11] Updated L is 3 after the official ESM/low-PAN and observed-only execution assessment. BQS and GQS are unchanged.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Software development, cloud, data engineering, AI and supply-chain/warehouse implementation services monetize engineering work and domain expertise. A large offshore delivery relationship with promoter Delaplex Inc and related Xperity creates both recurring access and dependence. UK Blueberry expands direct customer/platform capability; Bisham adds WMS consulting. BSNL micro-data-centre work is paid pilot activity, not yet a proven infrastructure annuity. [S1][S3][S5][S6]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Long-standing enterprise delivery, domain knowledge and exclusive related-US arrangements create switching friction. Yet FY2023 top-five concentration 98.51% and FY2026 related sales 58.21% constrain independent franchise claims. AI may increase delivery efficiency but also client bargaining power and reduce billable effort; management discussed spending pressure. Neither technology labels nor acquired products establish proprietary pricing power. [S1][S3][S5]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Parent revenue FY2021–26 isRs 36.22/49.74/54.00/55.35/55.76/56.77 crore, five-year CAGR about 9.4%, with recent near-stagnation. Group FY2025/26Rs 67.54/68.89 crore includes acquired Blueberry, so group long-run CAGR is not called organic. Domestic sales grew 49.3% while exports fell 15%. Core EBIT fellRs 13.05 to 12.32 crore; other incomeRs 4.18 crore includes interestRs 2.29 and FXRs 1.88. Reported PAT improvement is therefore not equivalent to operating acceleration. [S1][S2][S3]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Software/platform WIP Rs 13.98 crore, completed applicationRs 0.75 crore and goodwillRs 6.05 crore are substantial against annual core EBITRs 12.32 crore. Future monetization and useful-life/amortization assumptions matter more than generic IT market growth. Paid BSNL POCs and domestic diversification provide real options. September Bisham acquisition is completed for up toGBP400,000 plusGBP2 and costs, but revenue ceilings and no earnings disclosure do not establish attractive acquisition returns. [S1][S4][S5][S6]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: March promoter ownership 74.25% gives stable control but significant related-customer exposure. Group related salesRs 40.10 crore improved as a proportion from 68.24% to 58.21%; this does not establish arm’s-length prices. Actual named remuneration and family rent are disclosed in evidence, not confused with borrowing/related-party authorization ceilings. June options issued at face value dilute holders; annual narrative cancels 66,600 options while movement table says none cancelled. April exchange clarification corrected formats, EPS and proceeds disclosures. No severe diversion established; no blanket governance clearance. [S1][S7][S8] The May 28 March-utilization table now supersedes the older September position: ₹2.3605 crore remains, despite the cover letter’s broad statement that funds were used for their purposes. The detailed table and accountant certificate, rather than an inference that all proceeds were spent, govern the cash assessment. October 17 claims an SME reporting exemption; that is not evidence of superior governance. [S13][S16]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Two-year group CFO/PAT is 0.8785 x; FY2026 CFO13.8931 less reported capex 8.8005 gives FCF5.0926 crore. Closing cash 6.3115 reconciles. However asset-note purchases about 5.8945 crore are below reported cash capex by 2.9060; translation appears in asset movements and CFO adds 2.0233 crore FX translation. Removing both provisionally yields FCF sensitivity 5.9753 crore, not a certified cash measure. Platform purchases 3.4797 crore are capitalized; immediate expensing would reduce pre-tax operating earnings materially. WIP not amortized requires recoverability scrutiny. Goodwill increase 1.5412 is labelled currency revaluation; exact bridge remains unresolved, not proof of missing cash. Parent/restated historic CFO versions are retained separately. [S1][S2][S3] The complete operating-WC opening balance is ₹22.8353 crore after adding operating security/professional-tax assets and deducting operating salary/audit/expense provisions. Corporate income-tax balances and financial deposits remain outside WC. [S1]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At the official October 19 ₹155.70 close, current-share market capitalization is ₹142.60 crore and owner P/E about 11.11×. Full annual scenarios begin with actual ₹22.8353 crore operating WC, zero debt and explicit bank/FD cases, not assumed net cash. Base available cash is ₹23.2416 crore; all-deposit upside cash ₹41.9816 crore is conditional on availability. Bisham cash consideration and fees are modeled at ₹5.5 crore, varied from ₹5–6.5 crore; no unverified acquired earnings are added. Development/replacement capex, option cash/dilution, gross debt interest and tax are linked annually.  Severe asset/client impairment and cash/option/exit sensitivities are supplied. IAS remains NS because acquired earnings, current deposit restrictions and platform economics are not sufficiently bounded. [S1][S6][S7][S8][S9] Model correction dated 20 October 2026: the earlier forecast omitted certain opening liabilities excluded from operating working capital. The revised model pays opening net tax and other current claims once, preserves actual opening assets/debt, and leaves employee provisions already captured in working capital unchanged. This corrects our forecast, not the issuer’s financial statements. No liability is paid twice through working capital, debt, capex or recurring compensation. Corrected bear/base/bull terminal prices are ₹81.33/₹241.15/₹531.86; corresponding five-year returns are -12.18%/9.14%/27.85%. These remain conditional operating and funding scenarios, not executable entry prices. Opening-claim amounts, timing alternatives and annual cash/debt checks are in the model. [S1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Loss or repricing of the two related channels could damage more than half group revenue. A50% write-down of development WIP would beRs 6.99 crore pre-tax,54% of annual group PAT; no impairment is asserted. A severe scenario halves core EBITDA and values it at 6 x, adds only cash-on-hand after assumed acquisition payment and increases granted-option dilution. This is a stress, not a forecast or price floor. Conditional 60-session median supports only about 12.4 sessions to exitRs 5 lakh at 5% participation; ESM Stage I, large lots and unknown spreads/circuits can make actual exit much worse. [S1][S6][S9][S11] The severe annual model now replaces the former one-line haircut: debtor impairment reduces usable opening WC once; platform/goodwill impairment is noncash and added back, with reduced operating margins/growth reflecting lost productivity. Funding draws and half-year interest are explicit. Official observed-only liquidity uses 59 dates, not an assumed zero for the missing date; L is 3 after ESM/concentration caution. [S12]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold/five-year appreciation requires 38.0% annual per-share compounding, tenfold 58.5%. Present organic sales growth and core-earnings direction do not support those rates. A credible upside path needs independent customer growth, cash-generating platform adoption, successful acquisition integration and limited dilution. No probability or multibagger label is assigned.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Next results: independent versus related revenue, geographic growth, EBIT excluding deposit interest/FX, billable utilization and signed pilot conversions. Request platform revenue, useful lives, WIP ageing and impairment tests; reconcile translation between CFO and investing and confirm residual options. Track Bisham acquired earnings, consideration paid and integration costs; update restricted deposits and IPO utilization. Watch whether domestic growth offsets export weakness. Verify current pledges, bid/ask and ESM treatment before any position. [S1][S4][S6][S7][S8][S11]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Deep review completed across business, historical statements, related parties, cash classification, acquisitions, dilution, execution and scenario valuation. Medium-confidence quality scores are rankable; low-confidence investment attractiveness is not. Hold for evidence on organic demand, platform cash returns and unrestricted funds rather than infer cheapness from headline EPS. This research does not execute a trade.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions

FY2024 scanned statements were OCR and visually checked. Latest annual PDF initially truncated and was replaced with the full-size download. Unmodified audit/no disclosed pending group litigation is dated annual evidence, not independent universal clearance. Current pledge, deposit restrictions, precise FX cash classification, platform economics and residual option count remain bounded gaps. [S1][S2][S3][S6][S7][S8] Supplemental review includes May 28 IPO utilization, September AGM voting, September 26 completed Bisham purchase, October 14 price clarification and October 17 SME reporting exemption. Price clarification contains management’s disclosure assertion, not a guarantee of fair value. [S13][S14][S15][S16]

notes: Actual March balances underpin every case; deposit inclusion is explicit, not an arbitrary ₹30 crore cash midpoint. No IPO receipts are added again. Current deposit restrictions and use of IPO earmarks remain unverified.

Known June exercise receipt ₹0.04848 crore enters FY2027 financing once; its issued shares are already included in 9,158,480. Residual options 16,720–83,320 separately exercise at ₹10 with matching share dilution and cash. No authorized but ungranted pool is treated as granted.

Bisham consideration is disclosed as no more than GBP400,000 plus GBP2 for the second entity, excluding fees. ₹5 crore uses an analyst GBP/INR125 convention, not an observed FX fixing; a separate ₹0.5 crore fee reserve makes ₹5.5 crore base funding. ₹5–6.5 crore sensitivities cover cash/FX/fees, not an assertion of actual payment. No additional acquired revenue, profit or net assets are invented.

Revenue-linked capex includes development cash and replacement needs even where software costs are capitalized. Existing ₹13.9846 crore WIP and ₹6.0545 crore goodwill are not cash spent again. Severe impairment charges are noncash and added back, while lower growth/margin represent lost economic productivity. Debtor losses instead reduce usable opening WC and create replacement funding through delta WC once. No impairment tax shield.

Borrowing at 11% on opening debt plus half of draws minus half of repayments is solved simultaneously with 25% positive cash tax. Funding availability is conditional; cash floor ₹0.3 crore. Deposit income and separate terminal restricted-deposit recovery are excluded.

Terminal EV equals final EBITDA times the stated multiple; equity adds cash and subtracts debt. Dividends zero. Current ownership shares plus residual options determine per-share values and five-year IRR from ₹155.70. Owner equity applies the current group minority-profit fraction 0.0721/12.9111 as an explicit proxy, not a subsidiary valuation; the severe case uses 2%. A detailed subsidiary valuation could change the allocation.

Updated March utilization leaves ₹2.084 crore marketing and ₹0.2765 crore laptops. Forecast operating expenses are assumed to absorb the marketing allocation within stated EBITDA margins, and forecast capex includes the laptops; neither is deducted twice. No extra unspent-IPO cash is added because March bank/FD balances already include it. A failure to deliver these expenses within the assumed operating margin would reduce returns.

Model correction dated 20 October 2026: the earlier forecast omitted certain opening liabilities excluded from operating working capital. The revised model pays opening net tax and other current claims once, preserves actual opening assets/debt, and leaves employee provisions already captured in working capital unchanged. This corrects our forecast, not the issuer’s financial statements. No liability is paid twice through working capital, debt, capex or recurring compensation.
